newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU oil product stocks rise seen resuming in June.
newsitem.headline: EU oil product stocks rise seen resuming in June.

text.p: European oil inventory figures for the end of June, to be released on Wednesday, are likely to show steady or dipping crude stocks and an overall build in oil products, analysts said.
Almost all analysts questioned saw profit margins further under pressure in the coming month.
Distillate stocks are widely expected to have risen by two to four million barrels in June as European demand remained low and little product was drawn out of the region.
Russian supplies, some of which were diverted to the Asia-Pacific region in previous months, also pressured the market.
This could increase Europe's surplus of distillates, stocks of which ended May almost 20 million barrels above year-ago levels.
"We were already at record highs at the end of May," one analyst said.

Gasoline stocks were likely to be steady to slightly higher as reasonable trade into the U.S. at the start of the month was followed by buying into the U.K. later ahead of the budget. Britain increased duty on auto fuels by four pence a litre in its budget on July 2.

"Gasoline has been drawn down steadily since March and it would normally happen in June, but it probably flattened out, or even increased slightly this year because of the U.K. budget," one analyst said.
Crude stocks are seen flat to slightly lower despite reasonably heavy maintenance in the North Sea in June. Some analysts believe supplies of West African crude also found their way to Europe.
One contrast with May is that refineries were running at or near full capacity. Despite falling margins, almost no majors took the decision to cut runs.
In May, a number of observers were surprised to find that crude stocks had fallen, by 3.65 million barrels. A number predicted a sharp rise.
The figures for the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway will be published by Euroilstock at 1300 GMT on Wednesday.
